title: CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill
what_it_is: CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill

sections.label: MediShield Life universal health coverage
sections.summary: MediShield Life was implemented in 2015 to give all Singaporeans universal health coverage, including older Singaporeans regardless of age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In 2015, we implemented MediShield Life to provide universal health coverage, with better protection for all, so that all Singaporeans have peace of mind for their hospitalisation bills, and for life, so that older Singaporeans are covered, too, regardless of their age.

sections.label: Universal insurance for long-term care
sections.summary: Universal insurance coverage for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, regardless of health, disability and financial status, for long-term care costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: First, universal insurance coverage for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, regardless of their health, disability and financial status, so that our future generations will have basic protection against the costs of long-term care.

sections.label: ElderFund for low-income disabled citizens
sections.summary: ElderFund will be a discretionary Government assistance scheme for low-income, severely disabled Singapore Citizens aged 30 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: ElderFund will be a discretionary Government assistance scheme for low-income, severely disabled Singapore Citizens who are aged 30 and above.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawals for severely disabled
sections.summary: Severely disabled Singaporeans aged at least 30 can withdraw up to $200 monthly from their own and spouses' MediSave Accounts for long-term care.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Severely disabled Singaporeans who are at least 30 years old will be able to make cash withdrawals of up to $200 a month from their own and their spouses' MediSave Accounts to support their long-term care needs.

sections.label: Scheme covers citizens and PRs
sections.summary: The Scheme will apply to all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents born on 1 January 1980 or later.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In line with our vision for inclusivity, the Scheme will apply to all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents (PRs) born on 1 January 1980 or later.

sections.label: Auto-enrolment of younger ElderShield policyholders
sections.summary: Those born between 1970 and 1979 who are ElderShield policyholders and not severely disabled will be auto-enrolled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To encourage participation of younger cohorts of this group, we will auto-enrol those born between 1970 and 1979, who are ElderShield policyholders and are not severely disabled.

sections.label: CareShield Life launch dates
sections.summary: CareShield Life will launch around mid-2020 for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, and from mid-2021 for those born in 1979 or earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The new CareShield Life Scheme will be launched around mid-2020 for Singaporeans born in 1980 or later, and we aim to progressively launch the Scheme for Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier, from mid-2021, about a year later.

sections.label: Disability assessors and information access
sections.summary: The Bill lets CPF Board and AIC access disability-related health information to administer schemes and assess auto-enrolment eligibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To this end, we plan to double the number of disability assessors to about 300 by the launch of CareShield Life, and we are working with healthcare institutions to progressively expand the types of disability assessments that can be accepted for claims, so that policyholders need not undergo another disability assessment if we already have similar data on their disability status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To further provide convenience to policyholders, Part 8 of the Bill will enable CPF Board and AIC to access an individual’s disability-related health information and allow the information to be disclosed to authorised persons approved by the Minister, for the administration of prescribed public schemes, or provision of support to disabled persons for prescribed purposes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These provisions allow us to proactively reach out to disabled individuals to inform them of their eligibility for claims, not just for CareShield Life and ElderShield, but also for other Government disability schemes, using disability assessments already performed at our healthcare institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These provisions also allow us to access and use disability assessments already done at healthcare institutions to assess the eligibility of those born between 1970 and 1979 for the auto-enrolment exercise into CareShield Life without having to get them to be assessed again.

sections.label: Offence for wrongful information use
sections.summary: The Bill makes wrongful access, use or disclosure of any information collected an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Bill makes the wrongful access, use or disclosure of any information collected an offence.

sections.label: Protecting payouts from creditors
sections.summary: Clause 20 protects CareShield Life and ElderShield payouts from creditors, with two tight exceptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Clause 20 of the Bill protects CareShield Life and ElderShield payouts from creditors, with two tight exceptions.

sections.label: Premium subsidies and participation incentives
sections.summary: Means-tested premium subsidies, transitional subsidies and participation incentives of up to $4,000 for Pioneer and Merdeka Generation seniors will be provided.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For those who need help with their CareShield Life premium payments, we will put in place measures to ensure premiums remain affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: There will be means-tested premium subsidies of up to 30% to help lower- to middle-income Singaporeans with their premiums.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Transitional subsidies will be given to Singapore Citizens born in 1980 or later for the first five years from CareShield Life’s commencement to ease their transition into the Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For Singapore Citizens born in 1979 or earlier, they will be given participation incentives of up to $2,500, if they join CareShield Life in the first two years after the Scheme is available for sign-ups from mid-2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In addition, seniors from the Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation will receive additional participation incentives of $1,500, so that they receive a total of $4,000 in participation incentives.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawal limits for long-term care
sections.summary: Long-term care withdrawals are based on prevailing MediSave balance, up to $200 a month per severely disabled individual.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To ensure that members have sufficient MediSave balances for other medical treatments, the amount that can be withdrawn for long-term care will be based on their prevailing MediSave balance, and up to $200 a month for each severely disabled individual.

sections.label: Long-term Care Support Fund
sections.summary: The Bill establishes a $5.1 billion Government Long-term Care Support Fund administered by MOH, separate from the insurance fund holding premiums.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Bill provides for the establishment of a Government fund called the Long-term Care Support Fund in clauses 38 and 39.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This Fund will be administered by MOH and $5.1 billion will be set aside in this Fund, as announced by the Deputy Prime Minister during Budget 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: ElderFund is a new discretionary Government assistance scheme that will be implemented in January 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Long-Term Care Support Fund, or the support fund, holds the $5.1 billion of Government monies and is used to provide Government support, while the CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund – we call the insurance fund – holds the premium monies collected and are used for CareShield Life and ElderShield payouts and expenses.

sections.label: CareShield Life enrolment for older cohorts
sections.summary: CareShield Life is mandatory for Singaporeans born 1980 and later, optional for earlier cohorts, and the member asks about financial support for older enrolment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: CareShield Life will be mandatory for all Singaporeans born in 1980 and later, but will be optional for those who are born earlier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand that enrolling older Singaporeans into the expanded benefits schedule of CareShield Life would be costly, but would the Government consider further measures to financially support older cohorts to encourage them to either enrol or switch over from ElderShield to CareShield Life?

sections.label: Additional premium support criteria
sections.summary: The passage asks what the criteria are for granting additional premium support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What are the criteria for granting additional premium support?

sections.label: GPC payout adequacy concerns
sections.summary: The GPC paper acknowledged concerns about payout adequacy related to cost-of-living increases and medical inflation uncertainties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The GPC has acknowledged in our paper that there were concerns regarding the adequacy of payouts, related to uncertainties regarding the pace of cost-of-living increases and also medical inflation.

sections.label: CareShield Life transparency and administration
sections.summary: The member asks how much information on CareShield Life administration, fund management, premium pricing and payout disbursement will be released publicly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In concluding, I would like to ask the Ministry to what degree information will be released to the public regarding the administration of CareShield Life, and whether the Ministry would be transparent about how the fund is managed and how the premiums are priced and how payouts are disbursed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For instance, in the early years of ElderShield, it was found that claims were, in fact, below what was essentially projected, and rebates were, of course, duly given back to policyholders as a result.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This should certainly be happy news to policyholders at that time, but it also led to questions about whether the premiums and calculations were, in fact, overly conservative, and secondarily, whether this could have led to excessive profits gained by the private insurers who were then underwriting the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I look forward to the clarifications from the Ministry and I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This Bill is timely because one in two healthy Singaporeans aged 65 today could become severely disabled later in their lifetime, family units are becoming smaller, life expectancy is increasing and the population is rapidly ageing.

sections.label: Monthly payout inadequacy
sections.summary: The passage states that the $600 monthly payout is inadequate for severely handicapped individuals' long-term care basic costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One, the monthly payout of $600 is inadequate for severely handicapped individuals in long-term care basic costs.

sections.label: New long-term care assistance scheme
sections.summary: From 2020, a new scheme will give lower-income severely disabled Singaporeans up to $250 monthly for Long-Term Care costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: New assistance scheme from 2020 will provide lower-income Singaporeans who are severely disabled and need additional support for Long-Term Care costs of up to $250 per month.

sections.label: Elderly Singaporeans living alone
sections.summary: Singaporeans aged 65 and above living alone or with spouse but no children grew over 50% from 2010 to 2015, from 94,000 to 148,400.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The number of Singaporeans aged 65 and above living alone, or with their spouse but without children, has grown by more than 50% from 2010 to 2015 or from 94,000 to 148,400.

sections.label: Expanding home care programmes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MOH will support and expand the home care programme and other home care programmes, and asks the Minister to look into personnel supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I hope MOH will continue to support this programme and to expand it to other constituencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This home care programme emphasises on prevention of further deterioration of medical conditions or frequent visits to hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We also need to expand other home care programmes for complex long-term care needs in the community.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can look into the requirement and supply of personnel for such home care as soon as possible to expand this sector.

sections.label: CareShield Life inclusivity for disabled
sections.summary: The speaker asks about the fate of currently disabled Singaporeans under CareShield Life, saying case-by-case ministerial discretion gives no assurance of inclusivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: On the point of inclusivity, I would like to ask the Minister what would happen to the fate of Singaporeans who are currently disabled, mild or severe, when CareShield Life kicks in?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under clause 6, subsection (4)(b) of the proposed Bill, the CPF Board may determine that an individual who is severely disabled currently may be covered under CareShield Life, but only if the individual satisfies such conditions as may be determined by the Minister in any particular case where the Minister considers appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Such case-by-case basis assessment at the sole discretion of the Minister does not provide any assurance that CareShield Life is going to be inclusive for Singaporeans who need the basic protection most.

sections.label: CareShield Life premium pricing transparency
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Minister will publish the factors and assumptions in the CareShield Life premium pricing model for transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Would the Minister not agree that, using data that may not even trigger a claim under the proposed scheme to help calculate the corresponding premium to pay for an insured person would not be meaningful to begin with?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, in the interest of transparency on the affordability and sustainability of the scheme, would the Minister be able to publish a brief of the factors and assumptions made in the premium pricing model for CareShield Life?

sections.label: CareShield Life compulsory for citizens
sections.summary: CareShield Life, a migration from ElderShield, is compulsory for all Singapore citizens and PRs born on or after 1 January 1980 and at least 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The CareShield Life Scheme, which is a migration from ElderShield, is compulsory for all citizens and PRs of Singapore born on or after 1 January 1980 and are at least 30 years of age.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawal for care
sections.summary: From 2020, $2,400 per year may be withdrawn from MediSave with a minimum $5,000 balance, using the patient's or spouse's account.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One new change is that, with effect from 2020, there is a possibility of withdrawal of $2,400 per year from the MediSave account, subject to having a minimum of $5,000 in the account.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Minister did mention that patients or the disabled person himself as well as the spouse's account can be used.

sections.label: Enrolling severe disability cases
sections.summary: For those with two relatively severe disabilities at the most severe end, assistance or scheme enrolment could be considered.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It can be from the most minor to the more severe.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, perhaps for those with two disabilities, but they are relatively severe, at the most severe end of the spectrum, we could consider giving them the assistance or enrolling them in the scheme as well.

sections.label: Unfamiliarity with long-term care schemes
sections.summary: Many people remain unfamiliar or unsure about the long-term care schemes administered by the Government and the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Until today, although there are many schemes administered by the Government and the Ministry, in terms of long-term care, many people are still unfamiliar or unsure about what these schemes are.

sections.label: CareShield payouts and long-term costs
sections.summary: CareShield starts at $600 per month and increases gradually, and grants and the scheme should be used for long-term healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: CareShield is a scheme that can provide help to families and the amount is not insubstantial because it starts at $600 per month and will increase gradually.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, if we know how to make use of this assistance, we should use the grants and scheme for our needs as well as our families' needs, because the expenditure for long-term healthcare is certainly high.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How long is this amount expected to last to meet the needs of Singaporeans?

sections.label: Compulsory CareShield Life at 30
sections.summary: Soon the CareShield Life scheme will be compulsory for those turning 30.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Soon, the CareShield Life scheme will be compulsory for those turning 30.

sections.label: CareShield, caregiving and LPA
sections.summary: CareShield Life and the Long-Term Care fund will help bridge caregiving, and those covered from 2021 may also need to apply for LPA.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: What more can they do to have peace of mind that their children will not be left to fend for themselves when they are unable to care for them in the long run?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Thus, I believe the CareShield Life and Long-Term Care fund will play a pivotal role in bridging at least some aspects of the caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: First, for those who are automatically covered under CareShield Life from 2021 onwards, is there a concurrent requirement for them to also apply for the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)?

sections.label: CareShield Life premiums for low-income families
sections.summary: MP asks how low-income families' concerns can be addressed since CareShield Life premiums add to other premiums like MediShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Since details of the premiums are not yet announced by MOH, can the Minister share how and what may be done to address the concerns of these low-income families, as the CareShield Life premium adds on to other premiums like MediShield Life that the individuals must afford?

sections.label: Disability assessment costs and Merdeka enrolment
sections.summary: MP asks about a reference cost range for disability assessments, single-doctor assessment, and how Merdekas aged 60 to 65 can enrol in CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry then provide the public with a reference cost range for each disability assessment service and are there any requirements that prevent an individual from being fully assessed by the same doctor for all conditions on ADLs?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Lastly, apart from those who are turning 30 and would be automatically enrolled in CareShield Life scheme, there are Merdekas whose age is between 60 and 65 that hope to enrol for CareShield Life as well.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide more information on how the Merdekas can enrol for CareShield Life and what are the criteria for them to qualify if they had previously opted out of the ElderShield scheme?

sections.label: Bill provisions, ElderShield administration, Long-term Care Fund
sections.summary: Most Bill provisions were debated last year; Government will administer ElderShield from 2021 and $5.1 billion is earmarked for the Long-term Care Support Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Most of the key provisions for this Bill were debated in this House last year as part of the debate on the White Paper expressing recommendations for the ElderShield Review Committee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Subsequent to that debate in the House last year, the Government announced that the ElderShield scheme will be administered by the Government from 2021 on a not-for-profit basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: During Budget 2019, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced that a total of $5.1 billion will be earmarked for the Long-term Care Support Fund.

sections.label: ElderShield premium rebate feature
sections.summary: The ElderShield Review Committee Report states the premium rebate lets the three insurers return 50% of accumulated surplus to policyholders if claims are better than projected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The ElderShield Review Committee Report, in the context of the existing ElderShield scheme, states that the premium rebate is a feature that provides for the three insurers that administer ElderShield to return 50% for the accumulated surplus to existing ElderShield policyholders, if the actual claims experience turns out to be better than what was projected.

sections.label: Assisted living pilot in Bukit Batok
sections.summary: Minister Lawrence Wong described assisted living apartments with communal spaces, focus group discussions, and a pilot site in Bukit Batok next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: During the Committee of Supply debate this year, Minister Lawrence Wong said, "Typically, in such assisted living apartments, there will be more communal and shared spaces for residents to interact with one another.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the assisted living model is new, we will conduct focus group discussions to seek views on the proposed concept for assisted living in public housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We will take in feedback and views from the discussions and I am sure seniors will welcome such an option where the model will be sustainable for the service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We will work towards a launch for an assisted living pilot site for public housing in Bukit Batok next year." Sir, the assisted living model is new to Singapore but far from new abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A 2016 survey by the Lien Foundation and Income found that nearly 50% of almost 1,000 respondents were willing to stay in ALFs.

sections.label: Singapore health and life expectancy statistics
sections.summary: WHO 2019 reported Singaporeans' healthy life expectancy at birth of 76.2 years, total life expectancy of 82.9 years, and health expenditure at 4.5% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The most recent WHO World Health Statistics 2019 reported that Singaporeans enjoy a healthy life expectancy at birth of 76.2 years, the best in the world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We also have a correspondingly high total life expectancy at birth of 82.9 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Health expenditure as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) was 4.5%, in the bottom quartile of countries worldwide by expenditure.

sections.label: ElderShield severe disability risk
sections.summary: The ElderShield Review Committee Report states one in two Singaporeans aged 62 today could become severely disabled in their lifetime.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the ElderShield Review Committee Report states, one in two Singaporeans aged 62 today could become severely disabled within their lifetime.

sections.label: MediSave balances first quarter 2019
sections.summary: As of the first quarter of 2019, the CPF Board reported aggregate MediSave balances of $97 billion, about $25,000 per member account on average.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As of the first quarter of 2019, the CPF Board reported that aggregate MediSave balances stood at $97 billion dollars, or about $25,000, on average, per CPF member's account.

sections.label: ElderShield estimated premiums illustration
sections.summary: The ElderShield Review Committee report states total estimated premiums from age 30 to 67 for a non-subsidised 30-year-old male policyholder will be about $11,300.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The illustration given in the ElderShield Review Committee report states that total estimated premiums, paid from age 30 to 67, for a non-subsidised 30-year-old male policyholder, will be about $11,300.

sections.label: Nursing home care subsidy plan
sections.summary: The ElderShield Review Committee report states the Government plans to subsidise about 60% of nursing home care cost for a lower middle-income severely disabled Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ElderShield Review Committee report states that the Government today plans to subsidise about 60% of the cost of nursing home care for a lower middle-income severely disabled Singaporean.

sections.label: CareShield Life scheme provisions
sections.summary: This Bill establishes the CareShield Life scheme and measures for long-term care financing support for severely disabled persons, with higher payouts increasing over time and no cap on payout duration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CareShield Life, while a great innovation that will substantially increase access to long-term care, has changed the structure of healthcare financing in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Old age, too, but only to those who are lucky enough to see old age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill establishes and provides for the CareShield Life scheme and other measures to provide for long-term care financing support for severely disabled persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: CareShield Life will feature higher payouts that increase over time, with no cap on payout duration, to provide better protection and assurance against the uncertainty of long-term care costs if a person becomes severely disabled.

sections.label: Monthly cash grant for FDW families
sections.summary: A monthly cash grant of $120 is provided to families needing to hire an FDW to care for a family member requiring permanent assistance with three or more ADLs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One aspect which I would especially like to highlight is the provision of a monthly cash grant of $120 to families which need to hire an FDW to take care of a family member who requires permanent assistance with three or more ADLs.

sections.label: Ageing and long-term care costs
sections.summary: The passage states that ageing and rising long-term care costs pose future challenges, and notes ElderFund will provide payouts up to $250 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As our population ages and long-term care costs continue to rise, we will face increasing challenges to tackle these issues in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I noted that the ElderFund will be set up to provide cash payouts of up to $250 per month.

sections.label: Severe disability definition and mental health
sections.summary: The Bill defines severe disability as inability to perform three or more physical ADLs, which the passage says excludes mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Bill defines "severe disability" as when an individual is unable to perform three or more of the following physical ADLs: washing, dressing, feeding, toileting, walking and transferring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, "severe disability" remains too narrowly defined, as it excludes people with mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is especially troubling as MOH has announced that in financial year (FY) 2017, we have 12.4% of Singaporeans aged 18-74 who suffer from minor psychiatric morbidity, for example, anxiety, depression and related disorders, which is estimated to rise to close to 14%, or about 315,000 Singaporeans in FY2019.

sections.label: Schemes requiring severe disability
sections.summary: The passage lists multiple schemes whose eligibility criteria require severe disabilities for people to benefit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, multiple schemes ranging from IDAPE, Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance scheme, FDW or its replacement Home Caregiving Grant, ElderShield or its replacement CareShield Life, withdrawal of MediSave savings and ElderFund require severe disabilities in its eligibility criteria for people to benefit from it.

sections.label: Marcus losing support as moderately disabled
sections.summary: The passage states Marcus is considered moderately disabled and loses close to $1,250 worth of support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the eyes of our system and policies, Marcus will be considered to be moderately disabled rather than severely disabled, and the result is that he will lose out on close to $1,250 worth of support, which would have been a lifesaver financially, as that would allow him to consider a broader range of options like employing a helper or engaging private nursing services that will enable him to pass away at home peacefully with dignity as he would have preferred.

sections.label: AWARE research on family caregivers
sections.summary: The passage states AWARE research found care recipients who are moderately disabled spend close to $866 after subsidies monthly on care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An ongoing research conducted by the Association of Women for Action and Research (AWARE) of family caregivers reveals that their care recipients who are moderately rather than severely disabled, could spend close to $866 after subsidies, or 22% of their monthly household income, on average, on care-related expenses.

sections.label: CPF balances for older females
sections.summary: The passage states the 2017 average net CPF balance for females aged 60 and above was $69,732, about 24% lower than males.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2017, the average net CPF balance for females aged 60 years and above was $69,732, which was about 24% lower than that of males.

sections.label: Singapore long-term care spending report
sections.summary: The Lien Foundation report states Singapore spends 0.19% of GDP on long-term care versus the OECD average of 1.7%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the "Care Where We Are" report by Lien Foundation, Singapore spends only 0.19% of GDP on long-term care, compared to the OECD average of 1.7% of GDP.

sections.label: Gender-neutral premium pricing urged
sections.summary: The speaker urges that premium pricing be made gender-neutral in a national scheme meeting the needs of all in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a national scheme that aims to meet the needs of all in Singapore, Mr Speaker, I urge that premium pricing be made gender-neutral.

sections.label: Children with life-limiting conditions care
sections.summary: Studies estimate around 2,000 children with life-limiting conditions may need long-term care, but no policy like the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund exists for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Studies have estimated that we have around 2,000 children with life-limiting conditions in Singapore, who would potentially be in need of long-term care should they continue to stave off the threats on their lives brought by their conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, the Enhanced Seniors’ Mobility and Enabling Fund allows for seniors to apply for up to 90% subsidies for consumables like milk and diapers, but no such policy is in place for our young ones who may be similarly disabled, where their families face similar financial pressures for long-term care costs.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant not age-restricted
sections.summary: The speaker is glad the Home Caregiving Grant would not be age-restricted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this vein, I am glad to see that the Home Caregiving Grant would not be age-restricted.

sections.label: Mapping of long-term care schemes
sections.summary: The Cassia Resettlement Team's mapping exercise found at least 22 schemes relevant to Singaporeans with long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent mapping exercise conducted by the Cassia Resettlement Team, they found there are at least a total of 22 schemes, including the new schemes and excluding those which will be phased out, relevant to Singaporeans with long-term care needs.

sections.label: Family's chaotic navigation of support systems
sections.summary: A family and volunteers navigated about 10 stakeholders and multiple applications, and without citizenship the wife and three children moved back to her home country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The subsequent days were a chaotic navigation of our systems for both the family and the volunteers attempting to support them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They alerted, made referrals and continued to work closely with around 10 stakeholders, including the Family Service Centre, Residents' Committee, AIC, Social Service Office, HDB, Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, CPF, the regional hospital and other service providers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The volunteers had to help facilitate or lodge applications related to ElderShield, ComCare financial assistance, renewal of rental flat tenancy, medical escort and transport services, application to withdraw CPF savings, and extension of the wife’s social visit pass for her to continue as the full-time caregiver.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The entire process was made even more difficult because many of the applications required the doctors to provide their professional input on issues related to mental capacity, functional status and details on the medical condition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Without citizenship, his wife and his three children moved back to her home country.

sections.label: Centralisation, social compact, long-term care insurance
sections.summary: The speaker urges consolidation of schemes and says public long-term care insurance is designed on social solidarity, not just actuarial fairness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: I also urge for more centralisation and consolidation of existing schemes to provide support in a more streamlined manner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: I feel strongly that this Bill tells of the social compact we aspire towards, beyond the technical policy details. "Cheaper to be dead than to be sick in Singapore" still hangs off the lips of so many ordinary Singaporeans, especially the elderly and those who struggle to make ends meet.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: While actuarial fairness and sustainability of the schemes are important considerations, we must not forget that public long-term care insurance is often designed on the bedrock of social solidarity.

sections.label: ADL claims and $600 payouts
sections.summary: An elderly unable to perform three of six ADLs can claim $600 monthly for life, and the speaker asks what $600 can buy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, if an elderly is unable to carry out three out of six ADLs due to old age, stroke or dementia, including bathing, taking medicine, changing, going to the toilet, moving around and moving from bed to chair or to a wheelchair, they can file claims and they will be able to receive $600 in cash every month for the rest of their lives to pay for long-term care until they are fully recovered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, Mr Speaker, how much can $600 buy in terms of life-term care, be it home care, full-time domestic helper, nursing homes, community day-care or other arrangements?

sections.label: CareShield Life coverage and nursing home costs
sections.summary: CareShield Life's $600 monthly payout would give some financial relief, though lower middle-income families may still pay about $1,000 monthly for nursing home care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: If he had had coverage similar with benefits like CareShield Life, while it would not cover all the cost required for him, the monthly payout of $600 a month for as long as he is severely disabled would have provided some financial relief.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For some in the lower middle-income group, even with Government subsidies, they still have to pay about $1,000 a month for their parent's nursing home care.

sections.label: Compulsory CareShield Life for those born 1980
sections.summary: The Bill makes CareShield Life compulsory for those born on or after 1980 and those 30 years old on or after 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bills seeks to make CareShield Life compulsory for those born on or after 1980 and those 30 years old on or after 2020.

sections.label: Severe disability definition in First Schedule
sections.summary: The First Schedule defines severe disability as inability to perform three of the six ADLs set out for CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In terms of qualifying for payouts and disability assessment, the First Schedule in the Bill outlines the definition of a person with severe disability to be his or her inability to perform three of the six ADLs set out for CareShield Life.

sections.label: Older Singaporeans' choice to participate
sections.summary: Those born in 1979 or earlier are not compulsory participants and may choose to join; the speaker asks MOH how they will be informed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For older Singaporeans born in 1979 or earlier, CareShield Life is not compulsory and they have a choice to decide on whether they wish to participate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can MOH share how and when this cohort of older Singaporeans will be informed of the details of eligibility and the amount of premium they need to pay to participate in CareShield Life, if they choose to do so?

sections.label: Mental health and dementia assessment
sections.summary: The passage asks how mental health conditions and dementia will be assessed under CareShield Life's severe disability definition, which is based on ADLs emphasising physical disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With regard to the definition of disability, I also want to touch on the point of mental health condition because CareShield Life's definition of severe disability today is based on the ADLs with emphasis on physical disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How will mental health conditions and dementia, for example, be assessed?

sections.label: Long-Term Care Support Fund
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to establish the Long-Term Care Support Fund, a $5.1 billion fund announced by the Ministry of Finance in March to support CareShield Life premiums and long-term care financing schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill also seeks to establish the Long-Term Care Support Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance had announced in March this year that the $5.1 billion fund will provide Government support for CareShield Life premiums and support various long-term care financing schemes for disabled persons, such as ElderFund.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawals and fund eligibility
sections.summary: The passage comments on a CPF Act amendment for MediSave withdrawals for long-term care of severely disabled persons and asks about eligibility criteria and publicity for the Long-Term Care Assistance Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I would like to comment on a related amendment to the CPF Act, which is, to make provision for MediSave withdrawals for long-term care for severely disabled persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   I would like to ask about the eligibility criteria for the Long-Term Care Assistance Fund and its publicity measures.

sections.label: Lifespan and poor health years
sections.summary: A study by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation found average lifespan would be 85.4 years in 2040, with years spent in poor health increasing correspondingly.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to a study by the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation, average lifespan would be 85.4 years in 2040.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But the number of years spent in poor health would also correspondingly increase.

sections.label: Automatic enrolment into scheme
sections.summary: The passage supports automatic enrolment of citizens and PRs at age 30, notes exceptions for those born before 1970 and from 1970 to 1979, and asks how many would not qualify.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, it is a good move to have citizens and PRs automatically enrolled into the scheme once they reach 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that those born before 1970 will not be automatically enrolled and those born from 1970 to 1979 are only automatically enrolled under certain conditions.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My question is: how many would not qualify for automatic enrolment and how would we get them on board?

sections.label: CareShield Life and patients below 30
sections.summary: The passage welcomes the $5.1 billion CareShield Life as universal healthcare insurance for lifetime coverage and higher payouts, and asks about patients below 30 with severe disability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The introduction of the new $5.1 billion CareShield Life as universal healthcare insurance to ensure lifetime coverage and higher monthly payouts is definitely moving in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I understand that CareShield Life aids to subsidise the cost of long-term care for adults above age 30 with severe disability, what about patients below 30, such as paediatric patients with severe disability?

sections.label: Actuary on CareShield Life Council
sections.summary: An actuary with a statutory role needs a Practising Certificate from SAS courses, and the speaker proposes including a SAS Fellow on the CareShield Life Council.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An actuary with a statutory role, such as the Appointed Actuary of a Life Assurance Company or the Certifying Actuary of a General Insurance Company, is also required to have a Practising Certificate awarded after attending relevant courses run by the SAS locally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, with regard to section 37 of the Bill regarding the CareShield Life Council, I propose that when the Minister appoints the Council, can the Minister consider including a Fellow of SAS who is conversant with the financial management of long-term care insurance in the Council?

sections.label: Independent actuary on Council
sections.summary: An independent actuary on the CareShield Life Council could evaluate actuarial analyses, validate conclusions and probe safeguards against frequent premium rate changes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I understand that MOH has appointed an actuarial consultancy to compute the premiums and in time to conduct an evaluation of the liability of the scheme, having an independent actuary on the CareShield Life Council can help by evaluating the robustness of the actuarial analyses and computation methodology in light of this scarcity of data, validating the conclusions drawn from the analyses, probing for the safeguards the consultant actuary has built in to avoid having to change premium rates too frequently.

sections.label: Minimum sum figure derivation
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the minimum sum of $5,000 was derived so account holders still have money for other healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: From news reports, the minimum sum that is being looked at is $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Would the Minister explain how this figure was derived such that it ensures that the account holder still has money to pay for other healthcare needs?

sections.label: Expanding long-term care supply
sections.summary: Expanding long-term care services supply is important as severely disabled persons are projected to rise to 69,000 in 2030 from 29,000 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Another side of the equation is to expand the supply of long-term care services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is especially important as the number of persons who are severely disabled is projected to increase to 69,000 in 2030 compared to 29,000 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: That is about a 140% increase in demand for long-term care services or long-term care caregiver training.

sections.label: Singapore healthcare efficiency ranking
sections.summary: Singapore was independently assessed as second in the 2018 Bloomberg study on most efficient healthcare systems, with good outcomes and reasonable costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Singapore has been independently assessed as being second in the 2018 Bloomberg study on most efficient healthcare systems, that is, good outcomes but reasonable costs.

sections.label: CareShield Life Bill support
sections.summary: The CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill supports recipients and families by pooling risks and allowing spouses to tap each other's MediSave accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Through it all, the recipient of help is still valued and valuable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill helps to support them and their families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By pooling the risks among many in society, they may be able to receive more than they would have in their savings otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: By allowing spouses to tap onto each other's MediSave account, another resource to support each other through the difficult time is opened.

sections.label: Severe disability numbers rising
sections.summary: Severely disabled Singapore residents aged 65 and above are expected to rise from 29,000 in 2014 to 69,000 in 2030, with median severe disability lasting about four years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The number of severely disabled Singapore residents aged 65 and above is expected to increase from 29,000 in 2014 to 69,000 in 2030, more than double.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The median duration for which Singapore residents remain in severe disability is about four years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Yet, about three in 10 can remain in severe disability for a decade or more.

sections.label: CareShield Life automatic enrolment
sections.summary: From 2020, all Singaporeans born in 1980 or after are automatically enrolled into CareShield Life regardless of pre-existing conditions or disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: From 2020, all Singaporeans born in 1980 or after will automatically be enrolled into CareShield Life, regardless of pre-existing conditions or disabilities.

sections.label: Women losing out on earnings
sections.summary: Women tend to lose out to men in earnings and savings, partly because they exit the workforce early to care for their families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Moreover, women tend to "lose out" to men in earnings and savings, in part due to them exiting the workforce early to care for their families.

sections.label: Premium rebates for older women
sections.summary: The passage asks whether older and lower-income women could receive more premium rebates so they do not lose out even more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Could older and lower-income women receive more premium rebates so that they do not lose out even more?

sections.label: Rebates for healthy behaviour
sections.summary: The passage asks whether those who maintained good health past 60 could get reduced premiums or rebates to encourage healthy behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Healthy outcomes are not just important from a financial burden perspective, but because we love life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And therefore, for those who have proven to engage in healthy activities and maintained good health past, say, 60 years old, could their premiums be reduced or could rebates be given as a way of encouragement to reinforce this very positive behaviour?

sections.label: One in two disabled
sections.summary: Statistics show that one in two Singaporeans aged 65 and above will become severely disabled later in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Moreover, statistics show that one in two Singaporeans aged 65 and above will become severely disabled later in life.

sections.label: Caregiver Grant and Pioneer support
sections.summary: The Caregiver Grant gives $200 monthly and Pioneer Generation disabled get $100 monthly, aimed at elderly long-term care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, we introduced the Caregiver Grant worth $200 every month; and in the Pioneer Generation Package, we provide additional support to the disabled among the Pioneer Generation worth $100 per month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: All these various subsidies and support packages are aimed at better looking after the elderly and giving them long-term care.

sections.label: CareShield premiums rebate question
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Government could offer CareShield premium rebates or discounts to those who exercise and stay healthy after 60.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: To encourage people to stay healthy, can the Government consider emulating private insurers and offer CareShield premiums rebate or discount to those who actively exercise and stay healthy after 60?

sections.label: CareShield Life long-term care
sections.summary: CareShield Life provides better long-term care and protection for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Very importantly, CareShield Life provides better long-term care and protection for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: CareShield Life coverage and cohorts
sections.summary: The Bill makes CareShield Life universal for those born in or after 1980, while keeping it optional for those born in 1979 or earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, in terms of coverage, the Bill reinforces and strengthens inclusiveness by making CareShield Life universal for future cohorts of Singaporeans born in or after 1980.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For older existing cohorts of Singaporeans, which are those born in 1979 or earlier, we have kept CareShield Life optional for them as we acknowledge that the profile of this cohort, this group, is a lot more diverse.

sections.label: Auto-enrolment for existing cohorts
sections.summary: Those born between 1970 and 1979 who are ElderShield policyholders and not severely disabled will be offered auto-enrolment; those born in 1969 or earlier will not.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about encouraging existing cohorts who would not be auto-enrolled onto CareShield Life to join CareShield Life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: I will reiterate what Minister Gan Kim Yong has shared that individuals born between 1970 and 1979 who are ElderShield policyholders and are not severely disabled will be offered the convenience of auto-enrolment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For those born in 1969 or earlier, they will not be auto-enrolled, as their individual circumstances are far more varied, as I have explained.

sections.label: Waiving first assessment fee
sections.summary: The first assessment fee for CareShield Life claims will be waived to reduce policyholders' hesitation in claiming.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Beyond what Minister Gan Kim Yong has mentioned about increasing the number of accredited disability assessors to about 300, progressively expanding the types of disability assessments that can be accepted for claims and also proactively reaching out to disabled individuals to inform them of their eligibility for claims, we will also be waiving the first assessment fee for CareShield Life claims to further reduce any hesitation or reluctance that an individual policyholder might have in making the claim.

sections.label: Exemption from further disability reviews
sections.summary: Policyholders assessed as clearly permanently disabled may be exempted from further reviews.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, policyholders who have been assessed to be clearly permanently disabled may then be exempted from further reviews.

sections.label: New framework and assessor training
sections.summary: Revised training and guidance for assessors will help cognitively impaired policyholders more consistently qualify for CareShield Life claims.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under the new framework and revised training curriculum, assessors will be guided with more information, more teaching and learning, and will be more explicitly guided on the aspects that should be taken into consideration if a policyholder is suspected to be cognitively impaired, including whether the policyholder's problem-solving ability and memory impacts his or her ability to actually carry out the physical acts of the ADL.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This will result in cognitively impaired policyholders being able to more consistently qualify for CareShield Life claims.

sections.label: Four more AICare Link touchpoints
sections.summary: Four more AICare Link touchpoints will be co-located at Silver Generation satellite offices by end-2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To embed more touchpoints in the community, we will create four more AICare Link touchpoints co-located at Silver Generation satellite offices, and this will be done by end-2019.

sections.label: Long-Term Care Support Fund and ElderFund
sections.summary: The Bill sets up the Long-Term Care Support Fund, with $5.1 billion committed, to support ElderFund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill also sets up the Long-Term Care Support Fund, which the Minister for Finance has committed to set aside $5.1 billion to service this Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: ElderFund, the discretionary scheme for the lower income who are severely disabled, will be supported by this Long-Term Care Support Fund.

sections.label: Tiered payouts and two ADL criteria
sections.summary: Ms Anthea Ong asked about tiered payouts; lowering criteria to two ADLs would raise a 30-year-old's premiums by about one-third.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Ms Anthea Ong, in particular, asked if CareShield Life payouts could be tiered based on the extent of disability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: I think Ms Anthea Ong would also know that lowering the claims criteria to two ADLs would immediately increase the CareShield Life premiums of a 30-year-old policyholder by about one-third.

sections.label: Payout for 30-year-old policyholder
sections.summary: A 30-year-old joining in 2020 may receive around $1,200 monthly if severely disabled at 67 or later.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: A 30-year-old joining the Scheme in 2020 may receive around $1,200 per month should he become severely disabled at age 67 or later.

sections.label: Home Caregiving Grant disability criterion
sections.summary: The Home Caregiving Grant targets moderately disabled Singaporeans who need assistance with at least three ADLs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In response to Dr Lily Neo's query on the disability criterion and assessment process for the Home Caregiving Grant, I should explain that the Home Caregiving Grant is targeted at precisely that, the moderately disabled Singaporeans who require some assistance with at least three ADLs.

sections.label: MediSave for CareShield Life Supplements
sections.summary: Singaporeans can use up to $600 of MediSave annually per insured person for CareShield Life Supplement premiums.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As with ElderShield Supplements, Singaporeans can use up to $600 of their MediSave annually, per insured person, to pay for CareShield Life Supplement premiums.

sections.label: Government commitment to affordable premiums
sections.summary: The Government is committed to keeping premiums affordable through the provision of subsidies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Fourth, I would like to assure Members that the Government is committed to keeping the premiums affordable through the provision of subsidies.

sections.label: Opting out and premium refunds
sections.summary: An auto-enrolled policyholder who opts out before end 2023 will have premiums fully refunded under clause 15.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, if an auto-enrolled policyholder decides to opt out before the deadline of end 2023, which Minister Gan Kim Yong outlined, the premiums he had paid will be fully refunded and the mechanism that is being used is designed in clause 15.

sections.label: Additional Premium Support for Singaporeans
sections.summary: Additional Premium Support will help Singaporeans who cannot afford CareShield Life premiums, with status shared across CareShield Life and MediShield Life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Government will provide Additional Premium Support to Singaporeans who cannot afford CareShield Life premiums even after premium subsidies, MediSave and family support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: An individual's additional premium support status will be shared across both CareShield Life and MediShield Life so that an individual would not be put through the task of having to apply for Additional Premium Support twice over.

sections.label: Prefunded scheme design and premiums
sections.summary: The schemes are heavily prefunded, with CareShield Life premiums payable until age 67 and ElderShield premiums until age 65.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It is, in fact, hard wired into the design of the schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, as a result, these schemes are heavily prefunded, with CareShield Life premiums payable until age 67 or spread over 10 years for older existing cohorts, and ElderShield premiums payable until age 65.

sections.label: ElderShield Supplement premiums not differentiated
sections.summary: ElderShield Supplement premiums are not differentiated by race or genetic factors, and the Ministry will not allow insurers to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In addition, I would also like to note that ElderShield Supplement premiums are not differentiated by race or genetic factors, the same factors that Ms Irene Quay has outlined.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And my Ministry will not allow insurers to do so.

sections.label: Actuarial integrity and premium subsidies
sections.summary: Actuarial integrity should be the basis for scheme design, while affordability is addressed through means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If Members have seen the numbers that I have outlined, I would suggest that greater inclusivity also means ensuring that the actuarial integrity of the scheme in itself should be the proper basis for designing the scheme's terms and that in the long term ensures a fair long-term sustainable outcome.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will, however, address affordability separately, including the points raised by Members, through the provision of means-tested premium subsidies and Additional Premium Support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The means-tested premium subsidies are intentionally designed to be based on a percentage of premiums so that lower- and middle-income women will receive larger dollar quantums.

sections.label: Public accounts of insurance funds
sections.summary: The accounts of the CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund will be made public, with annual information on premiums and payouts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Minister Gan Kim Yong has explained earlier that the accounts of the CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund will be made public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will also publish relevant information on the premiums collected and payouts made for the CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund on an annual basis.

sections.label: Surpluses returned to policyholders
sections.summary: Any surpluses from excess premiums will be fully returned to policyholders for their benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, I should emphasise that if the actual claims experience was better than expected, in other words, to take Mr Png Eng Huat's point – if we were more conservative with designing the scheme, that if the premiums collected are more than what is needed, then any surpluses from any of these excess premiums will be fully returned to policyholders, for their benefit.

sections.label: Independent CareShield Life Council
sections.summary: The CareShield Life Council will be independent and will review and make recommendations for both CareShield Life and ElderShield schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The CareShield Life Council will be independent and will review and make recommendations for both the CareShield Life and ElderShield schemes.

sections.label: Fines for fraudulent assessment offences
sections.summary: Maximum fines and penalties for fraudulent assessment and misuse of payouts will be twice those for false declaration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Bill provides that maximum fines and penalties for the offences of fraudulent assessment and misuse of payouts will be twice the maximum fine and penalty for the offence of false declaration.

sections.label: Fines and refunds under clause 50
sections.summary: Clause 50(2) fines go to the Consolidated Fund, while clause 50(3) lets Courts order errant payees to refund payouts to the CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The fines and penalty structure meted out under clause 50(2) of the Bill is to be paid to the Consolidated Fund – the fines go into the Consolidated Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: However, clause 50(3) provides for the Courts to order the errant payee to refund payouts he or she has received into the CareShield Life and ElderShield Insurance Fund.

sections.label: CareShield Life IT system security
sections.summary: The CareShield Life IT system will be designed and built to stringent security standards, including restricting access, encrypting data and monitoring system activity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Some Members were concerned about the security of the CareShield Life information technology (IT) system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will design and build the system to stringent security standards, for example, by restricting system access to only approved users, encrypting data sent across organisations, and also monitoring and tracking system activity.

sections.label: MediSave withdrawals for severely disabled
sections.summary: MOH extended MediSave cash withdrawals to the severely disabled, initially limiting long-term care use to the member or the member's spouse.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As a first step, MOH has extended MediSave cash withdrawals to the severely disabled in view that their care needs are typically more intensive and higher.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As we recognise that the amount withdrawn can be significant, depending on the length of the disability, we have started by proceeding cautiously by limiting the use of MediSave withdrawals for long-term care to the member or the member’s spouse only.

sections.label: Five thousand dollar MediSave floor
sections.summary: The $5,000 floor for MediSave withdrawal ensures Singaporeans keep some savings for other healthcare bills while allowing immediate access for long-term care needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Mr Christopher de Souza, I think, asked about why set $5,000 as a floor for MediSave withdrawal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It has been set to ensure that Singaporeans have some savings to help pay for their other healthcare bills whilst at the same time allowing immediate access to MediSave for long-term care needs.

sections.label: Long-term care financing pillars explained
sections.summary: The different long-term care financing pillars and basic insurance schemes such as MediShield Life, Dependants' Protection Scheme and CPF LIFE should be explained holistically as complementary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We also need to set out holistically how the different pillars of long-term care financing support work together so that people, just as Members in this House have, will have a holistic view of the different schemes, the different support structures that exist in this space.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We should also explain how different types of basic insurance schemes, such as MediShield Life, the Dependants’ Protection Scheme and CPF LIFE, all serve a different aim and purpose, and perhaps a different constituency of people, but they are all complementary in this landscape.

sections.label: Support for CareShield Life Bill
sections.summary: The CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill strengthens the long-term care financing ecosystem and enables the key pillars of the financing framework to be put together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: At the same time, we have built up our long-term care financing ecosystem with the introduction of various new schemes based on the key principles of inclusiveness, affordability and sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill contributes to that effort, strengthens the landscape in that space and enables the key pillars of this financing framework to be put together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As we continue to build on those efforts, I would like to urge the Members of this House to give your support to the CareShield Life and Long-Term Care Bill.

sections.label: Women's longer life expectancy
sections.summary: The passage states that women generally have longer life expectancy, supported by outlined numbers and others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If you follow the numbers that were outlined earlier – and that is one set of numbers and there are others that support this proposition as well – then, you would know that women, generally – I do not want to say specifically – generally will live longer, longer life expectancy.

sections.label: Actuarially consistent scheme design
sections.summary: It states that equal premiums could mean men effectively pay for part of women's payouts, so the scheme is kept actuarially consistent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For a typical woman, that payout will last for a longer period of time, and so the assets of the common fund will be depleted more quickly as regards a woman than it is for a man.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: When that happens, if you pay the premium in equal proportions between a man and a woman, and the man depletes the resources in the pool at a lower or slower rate than the woman, then you can see that there will be a differentiation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And over time, that differentiation will result in the man effectively paying for part of what the woman enjoys in the context of this scheme, which is why we made the point earlier – I think in the previous debate, last year, Minister Gan Kim Yong also made the point – that we try as far as possible to keep the scheme's design and the terms of the scheme actuarially consistent.

sections.label: Scheme is not universal
sections.summary: The passage states that this scheme is not universal, though a universal scheme might raise different considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If the scheme was universal, there might well be different considerations, but this scheme, the way it is designed as the Member would know, is not universal.

sections.label: Future adjustments and scheme design
sections.summary: It states that more claims history, progress, information and studies will be considered in adjustments and possibly future scheme design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: With more claims history, with the progress of the Scheme and with more information and obviously more studies done, all those will be taken into account as adjustments are made, and maybe even the design architecture of future schemes considered.

sections.label: Premiums and support mechanisms
sections.summary: It states premiums continue until three ADLs are hit, but support mechanisms prevent dropout if a policyholder cannot pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On the first point, if one is not at the severely disabled stage, then yes, the premiums do continue until the three ADLs are hit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But if the policyholder is unable to support it, then, she has heard from the Minister and myself, the whole series of support mechanisms will kick in to ensure that this person will not suffer a dropout from the policy only because he is unable to pay his premium.

sections.label: Men's additional premium not calculated
sections.summary: The passage states no calculation was done on how much more men would pay, as that component was put in during design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How much more would men have to pay?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have not done this calculation simply because when we looked at it and when the Scheme was designed with actuaries, that was the component that was put in.
